question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.body: a Cloudflare managed challenge page ("Just a moment..."), 5,516 bytes, with cf-mitigated: challenge: the documentation host asks the client to execute a browser challenge before serving anything, to this datacenter IP with this user agent
decoded.support-site: GET https://support.toolsgroup.com/ answers the same 403 managed challenge
decoded.llms-txt: GET https://www.toolsgroup.com/llms.txt answers 200 text/plain: a hand-written company summary (key facts, platform, demand planning, supply planning sections) that names products and no API, endpoint, credential or MCP server
decoded.challenge: none in the HTTP sense: the 403 carries no www-authenticate header; the gate is the CDN's bot challenge, not the application's authentication
decoded.mcp: none: the entry lists no MCP server and mcp.toolsgroup.com had no address record on 2026-09-13, so no MCP request was made
decoded.api: none: the entry lists no API surface and the vendor publishes no API reference the registry could find, so there is no endpoint to probe

finding: ToolsGroup publishes no MCP server and no API reference, so the only machine-readable surface to measure is the documentation itself, and it does not answer a machine. With no credentials and no cookies, GET docs.toolsgroup.com/ answers 403 with a Cloudflare managed challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) and no www-authenticate header, and the support site answers the same; the gate is the CDN's browser check, applied to this datacenter IP and user agent, not the vendor's authentication. The one surface that answers is the marketing site's llms.txt, a hand-written summary that names products and no endpoint. Same challenge and same llms.txt as the entry's 2026-09-13 note. The finding is that every cell is empty: an agent arriving from a cloud network cannot read this vendor's documentation, let alone call an API it does not publish.

reproducibility.command: for u in https://docs.toolsgroup.com/ https://support.toolsgroup.com/ https://www.toolsgroup.com/llms.txt; do curl -sS -i -m 25 "$u" | head -c 3000; echo; done
